song.title: We’re Making Pancakes
song.author: Mark and Helen Johnson
song.summary: Fun to sing, great to perform and even better to eat! This positive song has a real feel-good factor, with scope for layers of sweet harmonies. Watch out for the sneaky modulation into the final verse, and remember... ‘Don’t put too much sugar on the top!’
song.teachingTips:
• This is a catchy, fun song. Encourage the children to smile and look at each other and their audience (real or imaginary!) as they sing.
  • Throughout the song, the voices need to enter on the second beat of the bar. Practise this so no one is caught by surprise! (It will be easier to breathe in the previous bar rather than try to snatch a breath during the crotchet rest on the first beat.)
  • Make sure the syncopation on ‘savoury or sweet’, ‘such a special treat’ and elsewhere is accurate.
  • For variety and added musicality, try out different dynamics for each verse.

resources.title: Creating A Jazz-Style Accompaniment
resources.content:
[{"key":"7d5697aa8d26cffb","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"
  • To explore polyrhythm
  • To create and perform an ostinato as an accompaniment
","title":"What’s achievable","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/green-star-1614702483w2iKm.png"}},{"key":"a052042a0ecff570","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Amplified sound system; backing track for this song; percussion instruments 

","title":"What you need","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/blue-wrench-16147025258WedI.png"}},{"key":"465d16951881b049","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

The introduction of this song is rhythmic and syncopated with a laid-back jazz feel. Using percussion instruments, compose a cool jazz-club-style accompaniment to the song. Split into three groups and allocate each a set of instruments (e.g. shakers, cabasas, guiros, congas and bongos). First, establish a steady pulse, perhaps by walking on the spot, clapping or patting the chest or knees, so everyone really ‘feels’ the vibe. Then clap the rhythms below, making sure each group is really secure with their rhythm before transferring it to the instruments. 

","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"9003e3fcc8b7cbc4","layout":"image","attributes":{"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/MusicActivities/musicactivities-creating-a-jazz-style-accompaniment-1616582501cytja.png","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"c31e04c39d244370","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Repeat each rhythm as an ostinato throughout the song, first using just the backing track, and then adding the voices. Make sure the accompanying musicians are sensitive to the singers and don’t drown them out! 

","title":"","noMargin":false,"background_color":null}},{"key":"0d3c737d2c7c20a3","layout":"icon-bullet","attributes":{"body":"

Try making your own percussion instruments using everyday kitchen objects such as saucepan lids, frying pans, sieves and wooden spoons. If anyone has an old washboard knocking about it will make a perfect guiro! 

","title":"Branch Out","noMargin":false,"image":"https://assets.sparkyard.com/uploads/icons/u1874-1614695090s5QJx.png"}}]
resources.summary: Compose a cool jazz-club-style accompaniment to the song using rhythms learned from the song lyrics.

resources.title: Pancake Maths
resources.content:
[{"key":"3c9a600c0b0c0be4","layout":"wysiwyg","attributes":{"body":"

Can the children come up with some maths word problems to do with making pancakes? For example:

  • If it takes me 3 minutes to cook 1 pancake, how long will it take to cook 4 pancakes?
  • There are 3 people in my family. I have made 15 pancakes. How many will each person get?
  • I like lemon and sugar on my pancake. My brother likes sugar and banana. My sister likes chocolate and banana. My mum likes strawberries and chocolate and my dad likes just chocolate. Make a tally chart to show the most popular topping.
","title":"","noMargin":false}}]
